name: Galerie im Alten Rathaus
kurzbeschreibung: The Museum Kitzbühel at Hinterstadt 32 showcases over 60 original paintings by Alfons Walde, 3,000 years of mining history, and scenic rooftop views.
preis: Adults €9.00, youth up to 18 years free
oeffnungszeiten: Summer daily 10:00–17:00 (Thu until 20:00); winter Tue–Sun 14:00–18:00 (Sat from 10:00); off-season Tue–Fri 10:00–13:00, Sat 10:00–17:00
beschreibung:
Overview

The storied Museum Kitzbühel – Alfons Walde Collection (in the context of the Galerie im Alten Rathaus) is located at Hinterstadt 32 in the heritage-listed historic town center of Kitzbühel. Housed in the town's former medieval granary and an integrated defensive fortification tower, this landmark serves as the cultural centerpiece of the famous alpine resort. The charming historic ensemble welcomes art connoisseurs, cultural travelers, and history enthusiasts alike, celebrated as one of the premier regional museums in the province of Tyrol. Across several modernized exhibition floors, the museum unites renowned masterpieces of Tyrolean Modernism with the fascinating saga of local mining and Kitzbühel's legendary winter sports heritage.

Route & Requirements

The historic stone building dates back to the 16th century and was subsequently adapted as a civic grain repository. The undisputed highlight of the institution is the world's largest permanent exhibition devoted to the life and work of acclaimed Kitzbühel painter Alfons Walde (1891–1958). The top floor displays more than 60 original oil paintings alongside roughly 100 drawings, sketches, and iconic tourism posters. Walde's luminous snowscapes, sun-drenched timber chalets, and dynamic skiing scenes defined the alpine aesthetic and brought worldwide renown to Kitzbühel. Beyond fine art, the museum chronicles three millennia of regional mining tradition—from Bronze Age copper extraction to lucrative silver mining—as well as the golden era of the Kitzbühel ski racing legends and the historic Miracle Team led by Toni Sailer. Authentic vintage skiing equipment and rare archival films document the valley's evolution into a world-famous sports metropolis.

Visit & Arrival

Museum Kitzbühel is accessible year-round with seasonal hours: during summer open daily from 10:00 to 17:00 (Thursdays late opening until 20:00); winter opening Tue–Sun 14:00 to 18:00 and Sat 10:00 to 18:00; off-season hours apply. Admission is €9.00 for adults, while children and adolescents under 18 enter free. Rail access: ÖBB train station Kitzbühel or Hahnenkamm, followed by a leisurely five-minute walk through the pedestrian precinct to Hinterstadt 32. Motorists take the B161 into Kitzbühel, with parking readily available at the Pfarrau or Hahnenkamm car parks.

Tips

Thanks to a modern passenger elevator, the entire museum is barrier-free and fully wheelchair accessible. Make sure to visit the ground-floor gallery spaces hosting rotating special exhibitions of contemporary alpine artists. A summer highlight is the open-air roof terrace on the historic defensive tower, offering panoramic views across the Hahnenkamm Streif run and Kitzbüheler Horn. Combine your museum visit with a stroll through the colorful pedestrian streets and stop by a traditional Tyrolean café.
